name: Idi Amin
summary: Army officer who seized power in Uganda in a 1971 coup and ruled as military head of state until 1979. His government expelled most of the country's Asian population in 1972 and transferred their businesses and property to supporters, ran a state security service that tortured and killed suspected opponents, and governed by decree and a military council. He praised Hitler, attacked Israel, and in 1975 called for Israel's expulsion from the UN.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The 1975 Land Reform Decree declared all land in Uganda public land (academic study).

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament was abolished in February 1971 and its powers passed to him and the Defence Council, so spending had no prior approval from an elected legislature (ICJ report).

capital-controls.rationale: In his 1973 Drum interview he treats Asians sending money out of the country as economic sabotage that government cannot tolerate.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia; no source opened in this pass records censorship of art for moral reasons.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (para 96) he rejects the excuse that colonised peoples are not ready for independence.

collective-farming.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia; his 1975 UN statement names a Community Farm Settlement Decree but does not say it replaces individual farms.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Ruled from 1971 without elections, which the ICJ report says were never allowed, while parties stayed banned.

death-penalty.rationale: Decree No. 3 of January 1973 let the Military Tribunal try any person on a capital charge, and the ICJ report records firing-squad executions.

delink-world-market.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (paras 120, 130, 135) he invites foreign investment and calls trade the best form of international co-operation.

democracy-best.rationale: Elections promised in 1971 were never held (ICJ report), and Amnesty reports he ruled as Life-President under decree.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and dress rules; his 1975 UN statement (para 133) claims equal opportunities for men and women, so the sources do not settle it.

dominated-front.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): his 1975 UN proposal (paras 110-112) is a third-world security conference to avoid super-power interference, not a common front against Western powers.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: In August 1972 he told soldiers he wanted the economy in the hands of Ugandan citizens, especially black Ugandans, and decreed the expulsion of Asians (academic study).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the ICJ report states he ended the state of emergency in force since 1969 in March 1971, so his suspensions were not made under a declared emergency.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about other international bodies (such as the EU, WTO, IMF or WHO) or about support, funding or reform without enforcement powers, and the statement now asks whether the UN should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1972 expulsion singled out Asians for their origin; a US embassy report calls it racist, noting citizen Asians were singled out for no reason except race, and the ICJ report documents the treatment.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested on a quotation reached through Wikipedia; the ICJ report documents the expulsion of Asians but nothing that settles whether a nation should consist mainly of one ethnic group.

force-without-un.rationale: Led the October 1978 invasion of Tanzania and occupation of the Kagera Salient on his own decision, with no Security Council authorisation (New Vision account).

head-commands-forces.rationale: Decree No. 1 of February 1971 made the Commander-in-Chief, himself, chairman of the Defence Council, and Decree No. 3 gave the military head of state all legislative and executive power (ICJ report).

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: As military head of state he abolished Parliament by Decree No. 3 of February 1971 and ran legislation himself (ICJ report).

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: His 1975 UN statement (para 82) says the struggle is now for economic independence, without which political freedom is meaningless.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In his 1975 UN General Assembly statement (paras 124-128) he calls Israel a bogus State created by colonial powers, says there was Palestine until 1947, and backs a single Palestinian state, while separating Jews from Zionism.

land-redistribution.rationale: The 1975 Land Reform Decree abolished landlords' rents and converted freehold into leases, but an academic study records only limited implementation and fears of land going to the well-connected.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The 1975 Land Reform Decree declared all land public and converted freehold to leases from the government subject to development conditions (academic study).

leader-cult.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia and Wikiquote; the reports opened in this pass state no position on honouring a leader.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: In the 1973 Drum interview he denounces prostitutes and says he will round up town women to be put to work in rural camps.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army under him overthrew the elected government in January 1971, abolished Parliament by decree and ruled through a Defence Council it dominated, the opposite of guarding the constitutional order (ICJ report).

minority-conspiracy.rationale: In his March 1973 Drum interview he says Asians were committing economic sabotage and cites currency found packed in biscuit tins at a mosque as proof.

more-religion-public.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and state patronage of Islam, which does not settle whether religion should play a major public role.

nation-first.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia, and ruptures with Britain and Israel and nationalisations (ICJ report, US embassy report) do not settle putting national interests ahead of global cooperation.

national-resource-control.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (para 83) he says African states are fighting for full economic control over their own affairs.

national-self-determination.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (paras 96-100) he demands independence for the remaining colonial territories, rejecting claims that colonised peoples are unready.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Took over Asian and British businesses and farms and allocated them to individuals, a role far beyond protecting people from violence (academic study of Uganda's business-state relations).

party-controls-media.rationale: Decree No. 35 of 1972 let the government prohibit the publication of any newspaper for a specified or indefinite period (ICJ report).

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about one government, party or regime, or about fighting corruption, not a general claim that most politicians put their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

population-transfer.rationale: Decreed on 9 August 1972 that Asians holding British, Indian, Pakistani or Bangladeshi status leave Uganda within 90 days (ICJ report); a US embassy report of January 1973 records the expulsion of some 50,000 Asians by his decrees.

premarital-sex.rationale: In the 1973 Drum interview he condemns loose living by women and says he banned the mini-skirt.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (para 123) he says his government has taken measures to restore Uganda's cultural values.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The ICJ report records rule by decree, a Military Tribunal trying civilians without counsel and government actions without legal basis; a later academic study states the country was governed through decrees with no rule of law.

property-fundamental.rationale: Expelled Asians and expropriated their businesses with no compensation paid, and nationalised British farms and businesses without payment (ICJ report; academic study of business-state relations).

public-ownership.rationale: Reversed Obote's nationalisation in 1971, cutting the state stake in leading companies from 60% to 49%, then seized Asian and British businesses in 1972-73 and handed many to individuals (academic study).

public-service-media.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia; the ICJ report records a power to ban newspapers but nothing on funding public service media free from editorial control.

racial-group-interests.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (paras 131-132) he urges black Americans to overcome divisions and says Uganda champions their cause.

racial-pride.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (para 132) he says black Americans should identify with the continent of their origin as other races take pride in their ancestral homelands.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Decreed the expulsion of Asians from Uganda in 1972; a US embassy report notes citizen Asians were singled out for their racial origin alone.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (paras 81-86) he endorses the New International Economic Order and just economic relations for developing countries.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested only on a Wikipedia article; no source opened in this pass records his view on judging policy by results.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (paras 94-95) he appeals to developed nations for technical and financial assistance to new nations.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia; the ICJ report records the abuses but not his view on legal accountability for them.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (paras 120, 130) he invites foreign investment into Uganda's land and resources.

separate-church-state.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested on Wikipedia and state patronage of Islam; the ICJ report's ban on churches in 1973 does not settle whether state and religion should be separate.

separated-powers.rationale: Parliament was abolished, the Military Tribunal took over serious criminal cases and the judiciary lost independence (ICJ report).

settler-state-colonial.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (paras 124-126) he says colonial powers carved Israel out of Palestine and that Zionists colonised the United States.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His decrees placed the Military Tribunal above ordinary courts, the judiciary was no longer independent, and the ICJ report records actions without any legal basis.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia; the academic study opened in this pass records seizures and reallocations but no direction of investment into strategic industries.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (para 130) he describes Uganda as non-aligned and open to any country on acceptable terms.

strong-leader.rationale: Decree No. 3 of February 1971 abolished Parliament and vested legislative, executive and military power in him, so he governed without legislative checks (ICJ report).

suppress-opposition.rationale: Decree No. 14 of March 1971 suspended all political parties and activity and made political processions unlawful, and the ICJ and Amnesty reports record arrests, disappearances and killings of opponents.

term-limits.rationale: Amnesty International reported in 1978 that he held office as Life-President, with no limit on his tenure.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Invaded Tanzania in October 1978, occupied the Kagera Salient, claimed it was historically Ugandan and declared it Uganda's ninth province (New Vision account).

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Amnesty International reported in 1978 that Uganda was ruled by Life-President Amin, with no election and no limit on his tenure.

widespread-small-property.rationale: His 1974 remarks, reproduced in a Ugandan newspaper article, say that since the economic war no one should own more than one business and that officers with many businesses will be dismissed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Nulled (later pass, 2026-11-12): the earlier answer rested only on Wikipedia; no source opened in this pass links welfare benefits to work.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: In his 1975 UN statement (para 86) he says some industrialised nations still depend for their prosperity on exploiting developing nations' resources.

notes:
Many of his public statements survive only as press reports or secondary quotations, and the text of his 1975 UN speech and the 1972 telegram could not be checked against a primary transcript (the UN record and press pages were unreachable). The initial order for the 1978 Kagera invasion is disputed. The extent of formal Islamisation policy is unclear from the sources reached. Most of his record concerns force, property and rule by decree; positions on the large majority of statements (e.g. markets, welfare, family, culture) have no recorded evidence and are left null.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 36 answers taken from it, 22 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent third-model audit; all 490 active items and the complete blank list reviewed without consulting previous answers. Two historical inferences are explicitly low. Three of ten priorities answered, one inferred. The UN text is Amin’s prepared address even where Kinene reads it; other Ugandan delegates are not automatically attributed. The Drum source is an archived anthology reproduction, not an original scan. Assertions of equal rights, humane prisons and protected property cannot erase the governing record. Land nationalization is personally defended, but its implementation was limited and the economic programme also retained African private enterprise. No blanket socialism or worker ownership is attributed. Refusal to restore Buganda’s royal power does not establish rejection of every form of regional autonomy. UN institutional expansion does not establish supranational sovereignty pooling. Community work camps do not establish self-governing cooperative society or a universal job guarantee. Neither industrial collapse nor investment directives establish an assessment of industrial civilization. Language nationalism does not establish minority-language support. Wildlife research found personally encouraged poaching, but not a recorded view matching the precise ecological statements. Technology remains unknown. The full-cover requirement, all recreational drugs, same-sex criminalization, scriptural law and broad religious policies are not inferred from dress restrictions or Muslim identity. Approval of Nazi mass murder is not Holocaust denial. Life presidency is not a position on unlimited competitive reelection. Nasur’s and newspaper editors’ claims are distinguished from Amin’s own initiatives.

claude-sonnet-5-5 later pass (2026-11-12, rules 5): every source is now tagged as the subject's actions or words, and answers that rested only on Wikipedia or Wikiquote were re-sourced to the ICJ 1974 report, Amnesty's June 1978 report, the US embassy report (FRUS), the 1975 UN General Assembly statement (checked in the UN General Debate Corpus text), the 1973 Drum interview and two academic studies, or nulled with the old answer kept in reviewHistory. Record answers cite actions alone. Answered from the record: the 1972 expulsion, rule by decree and abolition of Parliament, the life presidency, the 1975 Land Reform Decree and the 1978 annexation of the Kagera Salient. Themes searched with no recorded position: markets and welfare, family and sexuality beyond the Drum remarks, ecology, technology, courts beyond the Military Tribunal, immigration policy, historical memory and reparations.
